title: Differential latency bucketing and KV eviction policy for mixed-length dialogs
creator: Priya Khatri
description: We observe increased tail latency and sporadic GPU memory pressure for workloads with a high variance in prompt/response lengths (short prompts with long responses interleaved with long prompts). This ticket implements a differential latency bucketing strategy in the continuous batching scheduler combined with a KV eviction/reservation policy that reduces KV thrash and OOM risk while preserving throughput for medium/long responses. Goal: reduce p95 generation latency for latency-sensitive classes and lower OOM rate during bursty long-response scenarios without significant reduction in overall throughput.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for 'low-latency' bucket improves by >=15% on production-like trace (same seq-dist) compared to baseline scheduler
KV cache hit-rate for long-response sessions increases or remains within 5% of baseline while reducing eviction churn by >=20%
No increase in GPU OOMs in the canary cluster over a 48h window; total throughput degradation <=5%
Scheduler exposes a config flag to enable differential bucketing and a KV reserve ratio per latency bucket
Unit/regression tests and an end-to-end perf benchmark added to CI with synthetic mixed-length traces
technical_notes: Bucketing: classify incoming requests into 3 latency bands at admission (fast: target SLO 50ms token, normal: 200ms, heavy: >500ms) using a lightweight estimator based on prompt length, user-declared priority header, and historical avg response length per client-id.

Batch windows: schedule shorter flush windows for 'fast' requests (micro-window 2-5ms) and larger windows for 'heavy' requests to allow slot coalescing; use adaptive window scaling driven by observed slot fill rate and tail latency feedback.
KV reservation: maintain per-band soft KV reservations (e.g., 10% of slot-kv-budget for 'fast', 60% for 'heavy') and implement a token-bucket style allocator to grant KV tokens at admission time.

Eviction policy: introduce time-aware LRU with hysteresis — prefer evicting KV segments associated with cold client-ids, avoid evicting prefix KV for requests within the same session; add a KV pinning signal for mid-merged responses that are likely to be resumed.

GPU memory hints: integrate with slab allocator to reserve transient small slabs for 'fast' band to avoid slab fragmentation by heavy sequences; expose per-GPU watermark metrics for reclamation triggers.
Preemption: allow preemption/slot-stealing of queued 'heavy' requests if a critical 'fast' request arrives and cannot meet SLO, bounded by a preemption budget to keep throughput predictable.

Observability: add metrics (per-band p50/p95/p99, kv_eviction_churn, kv_hit_rate_by_band, gpu_slab_fragmentation, preemption_count) and tracing tags for admission classification to correlate with console dashboards.
Simulation: we have a lightweight simulator implemented in python to model different bucket ratios and reservation levels against replayed traces.
Rollout: behind a runtime config flag with staged canary (10% traffic -> 30% -> 100%) and automated rollback on SLO regressions
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Spike completed. Built admission classifier prototype and scheduler simulator; validated bucketing reduces p95 for simulated bimodal traces by ~18% in the simulator.
2026-03-11: Implemented admission hook and per-request metadata tagging in staging runtime; added initial metrics (band assignment, slot latency).
2026-03-12: Integrated KV token-bucket allocator prototype; benchmark shows a 22% reduction in eviction churn on synthetic mixed-length workload when reservation enabled.
2026-03-13: Performance test uncovered increased fragmentation on GPU slab allocator under heavy reservation; added slab hinting integration PR to address fragmentation (see links).
2026-03-14: Running 24h canary against dedicated-staging cluster at 10% traffic. Early p95 improvements for 'fast' bucket ~16%, overall throughput down 2%. Monitoring KV churn metrics and OOM alerts.
Blockers: need kernel-level allocator metrics from infra to fine-tune slab thresholds (requesting infra instrument ticket).
